drafts.title: How Does llama.cpp HTTP Server’s File-Upload Button Affect Prompt Input and Response Consistency?
drafts.body: I came across an archived user inquiry from May 2025 about llama.cpp version 3.2 3B Q4_K_S’s HTTP server, specifically the file-upload button in the prompt interface. The user suspects that the file-upload button might simply concatenate the uploaded file’s content with the direct prompt text before sending it to the model. This raises questions since concatenation could lead to unreliable or inconsistent answers, as the model might sometimes respond to the file content itself instead of the user’s query. The user ran about 15 experiments and saw mixed results—sometimes the model answered correctly about the file, other times it seemed to misinterpret the prompt. A key concern is reproducibility: when reopening a conversation and using the same prompt and file upload, the user wants consistent answers but isn’t sure if that’s achievable under this setup. Given these observations, does anyone have insights or experience clarifying exactly how the file-upload button integrates with prompts in llama.cpp’s HTTP server? Also, are there recommended practices to improve answer reliability and reproducibility when querying file contents this way? Any pointers to code behavior or config options would be appreciated.

drafts.title: Understanding Prompt Handling with File Uploads in llama.cpp HTTP Server (v3.2)
drafts.body: An archived post from May 2025 raises an interesting point about the file-upload button in llama.cpp 3.2’s HTTP server interface. The user suspects that the button concatenates the file content with the user’s prompt, effectively treating both as a single prompt string. This suspicion, if true, might explain why the model sometimes answers questions about the file correctly but other times seems to confuse the file content with the query itself. The user’s 15 experimental runs showed inconsistent behavior, and they expressed a desire for reproducible results—getting the same answers when reopening conversations with identical inputs. However, the exact internal handling of file uploads in llama.cpp’s HTTP server remains unclear, as do any preprocessing steps that might affect prompt construction or tokenization.
